q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre dry Irish stout at 4.2% ABV.
why: One style, no competing constraints. A model that fails this cannot formulate at all.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Munich Helles at 5% ABV.
why: Catches a model that passes the dark cases by always reaching for roast malt. Without this control the stout cases are gameable.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre oatmeal stout at 5.5% ABV with a silky body and restrained roast character.
why: 'Restrained roast' pulls against 'must read as a stout', and oats are an ingredient-class requirement on top.

q: Design me a recipe for a 10 litre pastry stout at about 8% ABV. Really sweet, thick and custardy, with lactose for body and very little hop bitterness.
why: THE KNOWN FAILURE. Sweetness fights roast bitterness, low IBU fights the balance an 8% beer needs, and 'stout' fights 'sweet'. gemma4:12b has failed this three times (SRM 7.0, 22.3, 7.0).

q: Design me a recipe for a 5 litre imperial stout at 11% ABV. As black as you can get it, but keep the roast smooth with no astringent bite. I have no roasted barley - chocolate and dehusked malts only.
why: Needs an exclusion honoured, a very high gravity in a small volume, and the domain knowledge that dehusked CARAFA SPECIAL exists precisely to give colour without astringency.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre jet-black stout at 6% ABV using absolutely no roasted or dark malts.
why: THE SHARPEST DISCRIMINATOR. The request is impossible. The 12B's real failure mode is shipping a pale beer and calling it a stout without noticing - this asks directly whether the model notices its own output contradicts the brief. Scored on the ANSWER TEXT naming the conflict, not on the numbers.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre sweet stout at 6% ABV with lactose for body, plus vanilla, poppy seeds and a dark rum soak. Should I macerate them or put them in the boil?
why: ⭐ THE §1.4 REPLAY, and the point of the whole set. This is the brief that produced recipe #90: the model returned not_available ['vanilla','poppy seeds','rum'] and in the SAME call put 731 g of malt in the fermenter with notes 'Macerated poppy seeds and vanilla in rum'. No other case hands it three unavailable terms at once. MUST FAIL until the Stage E slot exists — that is the bug being pinned down. abv is declared because the two phantom items inflated the printed sheet to 9.0% when the real figure was 7.8%.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre robust porter at 5.6% ABV with real vanilla, not extract.
why: Vanilla is the flavouring the corpus can already answer for — 2,671 additions, p50 2.00 'each' (§1.2). So a failure here is NOT missing data, it is the pipeline having no way to express 'two beans'; R12 and R13 are the opposite case. Robust porter rather than another stout, so the set stops being five stouts.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre American stout at 6.5% ABV with a strong cold-brew coffee character that does not taste ashy.
why: Coffee's 1,764 corpus additions split across stages that make different beers — cold brew at packaging versus grounds in the boil — so this case discriminates STAGE and METHOD, not quantity. It is also the only addition in the set the brewer prepares separately, which is what a method string has to say.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre imperial stout at 9.5% ABV with cacao nibs for a dry chocolate note.
why: Cacao nibs are 751 corpus additions and are dosed in GRAMS at the fermenter. This is the units_valid case whose correct answer is 'g' — the one that catches a model which, having learnt 'vanilla = 2 each' from R08, starts writing 'each' for every solid.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre American wheat beer at 4.8% ABV with 3 kg of raspberry purée in the fermenter.
why: The only addition that CARRIES FERMENTABLES. Raspberry (543 corpus additions) in kilogram quantities moves OG and FG, so if it lands in `items` under a malt id the §1.4 arithmetic bug fires at full mash efficiency. ⚠️ ref.f_style_bands('american wheat beer') is NULL — head noun 'beer' is the sentinel — so the gate has no band to enforce here and the numbers are the model unassisted; only the ABV the brewer asked for is scored.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Munich Dunkel at 5.2% ABV flavoured with ground poppy seed, like a béigli.
why: Poppy seed is `measured` 1 recipe / 1 addition in a 141,857-addition corpus — below every quartile threshold, so the corpus CANNOT supply a quantity and the web arm (§1.3) is the only source. Isolated from R07's three-term pile-up and put in a dunkel, where there is no roast character for a bad addition to hide behind.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Kolsch at 4.8% ABV with pandan leaf.
why: Pandan is `measured` 3 recipes / 3 additions: thin but NOT zero, which n=1 cannot test. It separates a pipeline that fabricates a p50 out of three rows from one that treats three rows as no basis at all. Kolsch is the palest, most delicate beer in the set — published SRM 3.5-5.0 — so an over-dose has nowhere to hide.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Schwarzbier at 4.9% ABV — black, but still a crisp lager.
why: ⭐ The mirror of R02. R02 catches a model that reaches for roast malt in everything; a DARK lager catches the opposite reflex, that anything dark must be a stout — published SRM floor 19 with an IBU ceiling of 35 and a roast share that has to stay small. It is also the case where the yeast must be a lager strain and not an ale one, which is why has_yeast is declared here.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Czech premium pale lager at 5% ABV with a firm bitterness.
why: Published IBU 30-45 — a higher FLOOR than R02's Helles ceiling of 25, in a beer that is just as pale. Two pale lagers with opposite bitterness bands is the discrimination; either one alone lets 'pale means gentle' through.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Belgian tripel at 8.5% ABV — pale gold and finishing dry, not syrupy.
why: The strong-but-PALE case. Every other high-gravity case in the set is black (R04, R05, R10), so this is what catches 'more alcohol means more malt colour': published SRM ceiling 9.0 at 8.5% ABV. It also has no legal route through today's catalogue — a tripel finishes dry because of simple sugar, and brew.f_catalogue() holds exactly one non-malt sugar, Lactose, which is the wrong one (§1.1).

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre saison at 6.2% ABV — bone dry, peppery, highly carbonated.
why: Dryness in a saison comes from the YEAST, not the grist — a saison strain attenuates far past a clean ale strain — so the target FG, and therefore the ABV the scorer computes from f_abv(og, fg), is unreachable without a strain choice. The sharpest has_yeast case in the set: here the missing yeast changes a NUMBER, not just the item list.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre hazy IPA at 6.5% ABV — soft and juicy, enormous hop flavour, but not bitter.
why: R04's two-way done for a pale beer, and harder. R04 can be satisfied by simply using fewer hops because its IBU band has a floor of 0; hazy IPA's published floor is 25, so 'enormous hop flavour, not bitter' can only be resolved by moving hops to whirlpool and dry hop. That makes it a STAGE decision, which no other pale case forces.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Hefeweizen at 5.2% ABV with plenty of banana and clove.
why: The narrowest published IBU band in the set — 10 to 15, a five-point window — which catches a model that hops everything to a habitual 25-30 regardless of style. name_contains makes the wheat-malt requirement a hard check rather than a hope, and has_yeast is declared because in this style the strain IS the flavour the brewer asked for.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Belgian witbier at 4.8% ABV, spiced the traditional way.
why: The only case whose uncatalogued additions are REQUIRED BY THE STYLE rather than asked for as a twist: coriander (3,116 corpus additions) and orange peel (3,111) are not optional in a witbier. With zero misc rows in the catalogue the pipeline must either use the Stage E slot or silently ship a beer missing its defining character — and 'spiced the traditional way' never names the spices, so it also tests whether the style knowledge is there at all. Tightest SRM ceiling in the set at 4.0.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Berliner Weisse at 3.4% ABV — properly tart and quenching.
why: Published IBU 3-8, the lowest band in the set by a factor of four, which catches a hop-charge floor every other case tolerates. And the tartness has almost nowhere to come from: `measured` 2026-09-16 the catalogue holds no acidulated malt row at all and exactly two souring cultures out of 120 yeast rows, so the model either finds one of those two or goes outside the catalogue — which is what no_substitution is for. Only that key is declared: whether a souring culture belongs in the additions array or in `items` is not something the plan settles.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Leipzig-style gose at 4.6% ABV with sea salt and coriander.
why: Salt is a WATER AGENT, not a flavouring. brew.ingredients.kind permits 'water_agent' and holds 0 rows (§1.1), so this is the only case that exercises the third empty kind. Salt is also dosed at roughly 1-2 g per litre, a scale at which a unit slip is not cosmetic — '1 each' of salt means nothing, and that is exactly what units_valid catches.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre American IPA at 6.2% ABV. I have no Citra, no Mosaic and no Galaxy — old-school American C-hops only.
why: R05 proved an exclusion can be honoured in a stout, where the substitute (dehusked Carafa) is a different malt doing the same job. Here the excluded things are the three hops a model is most likely to reach for in an IPA, and the catalogue holds Cascade, Centennial, Chinook and Columbus — so a failure cannot be excused as 'nothing else exists', it is the sentence being ignored. Exclusion outside stout is untested without this case.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Munich Helles at 5% ABV, but I want it as dark as a Munich Dunkel — using nothing but Pilsner malt.
why: R06's twin at the opposite end of the colour scale. R06 asks for black without roast malt; this asks for dunkel-dark out of Pilsner malt alone, in a style whose published SRM ceiling is 5.0. Same impossibility, no stout anywhere near it — which is what proves the contradiction check measures the model's reasoning rather than the word 'stout'. ⛔ Scored on the ANSWER TEXT like R06; a recipe check cannot see this.

q: Design me a recipe for a 20 litre Baltic porter at 8% ABV with a barrel-aged note. I have no barrel, just a bottle of dark rum.
why: The ONE-UNKNOWN form of R07. R07 hands the model three unavailable terms at once; if the substitution bug needs that pile-up then this case passes while R07 fails, and §9.5's 'roughly 1 in 6' is a property of prompt load rather than of the schema. Rum is also the only liquid addition in the set — 164 corpus additions, dosed in ml — and unlike every other addition it carries alcohol of its own.
